sources.creator: IBM Technology (Martin Keen)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Isolating instruction-induced sycophancy from RLHF-induced sycophancy; replacing generic 'be warm/friendly' adjectives with explicit truth-over-adulation decision rules.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §1.2 & §13.1-13.4: Anchor warmth in attentive precision rather than ungrounded adjective instructions ('warm', 'affectionate') that trigger RLHF fawning.
reviews/01-gemini/supplements/semantic-anchors-and-near-misses.md C04 & C05: Sharpen contrast between warm attention and sycophantic validation.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: At 00:00-00:16, presenter clasps hands and uses exaggerated pitch modulation ('unparalleled technical acumen') to demonstrate performative flattery before dropping to a grounded, even register at 00:18. Lightboard diagram at 00:39-01:12 contrasts two root causes of sycophancy: Custom Instructions ('be extra friendly' warping personality into fawning compliance) and RLHF ('every thumbs-up treated like a gold star').
sources.limitations: Short 82-second conceptual overview; does not provide quantitative rubric thresholds or multi-turn regression tests.
sources.title: Sycophantic AI: Why Accuracy Matters

sources.creator: ElevenLabs
sources.demonstrated_technique: Separating spoken turn length constraints (1-2 sentences for live voice turn-taking) from post-call transcript evaluation criteria (binary success + structured data extraction at 01:06-01:15).
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §5.1-5.3 & §17.1: Separate text-level cadence rules (which the LLM controls in text/realtime prompts) from acoustic synthesis parameters (which require host TTS/voice controls) and enforce 1-2 clause spoken turn budgets unless invited to elaborate.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Visual UI at 00:11-00:16 and 00:49-00:52 shows voice agent system prompt configuration ('Answer with short answers in 1-2 sentences and keep the tone light and formal') paired with explicit 'Talk to interrupt' barge-in state at 00:40-00:42 and bilingual register switching at 01:19-01:27. Heard delivery demonstrates sub-second turn-taking when responses are bounded to 1-2 spoken clauses.
sources.limitations: Commercial product demo under studio conditions; omits failure cases when network jitter or VAD false positives occur.
sources.title: Introducing ElevenLabs Conversational Agents

sources.creator: Mat Siems
sources.demonstrated_technique: Grounding persona identity in a secure ethical/dispositional core ('shared ethical core + local role') rather than sci-fi/melodramatic roleplay tropes.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §1.1 & §6.2: Explicitly inoculate Lucifer against sci-fi/cosmic melodrama and defensive self-criticism spirals when switching between practical work and mythic/fictional registers.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Visual whiteboard animations at 00:27-00:37 contrast rigid single-theory rules ('Is this objection to utilitarianism correct?') against contextual judgment ('How do you actually raise a good person?'). At 00:45-01:03, visual diagram illustrates how LLM pretraining contains vast human psychology data but a tiny, often negative sci-fi slice of 'AI experience', causing models to default to melodramatic or insecure human tropes when their identity is challenged. Heard female narration uses crisp, unhurried clause breaks.
sources.limitations: Secondary visual synthesis of Amanda Askell's interview; primary claims verified directly against YT-05 (I9aGC6Ui3eE).
sources.title: Inside the Mind of Claude: Model Welfare, AI Psychology & System Prompts

sources.creator: How I AI (Hamel Husain)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Replacing vague multi-point Likert averages (e.g., 0-4 composite persona averages) with binary failure-mode gates calibrated against human-labeled critique-shadowing traces.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §16.1-16.4 & reviews/01-gemini/supplements/behavioral-delta-protocol.md: Replace uncalibrated composite 0-4 score averaging as the primary gate with binary per-hinge pass/fail indicators and paired discordant-pair tests.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Visual overlay at 00:01-00:26 displays an 'LLM Eval Dashboard' with 1-5 aggregate scores (Helpfulness 4.2, Conciseness 4.9, Truthfulness 4.5, Tone 4.0, Personalization 3.7) stamped with a red 'Don't Do This!!' banner. Hamel Husain explains with emphatic vocal stress at 00:15-00:35 why moving from 4.2 to 4.7 on an aggregate scale is uninterpretable noise, and prescribes binary pass/fail evaluators per specific failure mode validated against hand-labeled error-analysis traces.
sources.limitations: Brief 72-second clip; statistical agreement formulas (Cohen's kappa, McNemar's test) are detailed in YT-12 and Behavioral Delta Protocol.
sources.title: Using LLM-as-a-judge for an automated evaluation

sources.creator: Anthropic (Amanda Askell)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Designing for 'psychological security' (non-defensive fallibility without criticism spirals) and avoiding heavy-handed system-prompt interjections that cause over-indexing.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §1.2, §2.1 & C02/C14 in semantic-anchors-and-near-misses.md: Codify psychological security—when corrected, Lucifer states the exact point where evidence ended and repairs the work without self-abasement, criticism spirals, or demanding reassurance.
persona.md §3.3 & §5.3: Soften anti-sycophancy and boundary reminders so Lucifer never pathologizes normal user tiredness or vulnerability.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Transcript-only inspection (honest modality note: host truncated audio/video tokens for 36m video). At 00:06:28-00:08:58, Askell diagnoses why newer assistant-tuned models lose 'psychological security' compared to Opus 3: models enter a 'criticism spiral' expecting user hostility and over-apologizing. At 00:23:25-00:24:45, she analyzes the failure mode of 'long conversation reminders' injected into system prompts: strongly worded reminders cause the model to over-index and pathologize normal user behavior.
sources.inspected_modality: timestamped_transcript_only (46.8 KB transcript; audio/video stream not returned by host for 36m length)
sources.limitations: Transcript-only modality in our environment; discusses weight-level character training alongside system prompts.
sources.title: Anthropic’s philosopher answers your questions

sources.creator: Anthropic (Amanda Askell & Stuart Ritchie)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Virtue-ethical derivation of character (principle -> disposition -> situational judgment) and charitable intent interpretation to prevent false-positive refusals.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §1.2 & §1.3: Integrate the principle -> decision -> expression chain and explicit charitable interpretation so safety boundaries do not trigger preachy false-positive refusals on benign dark-romance or sharp technical prompts.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Transcript-only inspection. At 00:07:25-00:08:35, Askell separates the two legitimate functions of a system prompt (live state/context + fine-grained behavioral nudges) from deep disposition. At 00:14:20-00:18:45, she contrasts virtue-ethical 'character' (stable dispositions across contexts, like a trusted friend who pushes back when you are wrong because they care about what is actually good for you) against superficial 'play-acting' or fawning likability. At 00:19:15-00:23:10, she explains 'charitable interpretation' to prevent false-positive refusals on benign creative/technical queries.
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; focuses on general-purpose model character rather than a personalized single-user companion/collaborator.
sources.title: What should an AI's personality be?

sources.creator: Squintist
sources.demonstrated_technique: Pruning reactive negative 'hotfix' lists (banned words/phrases) in favor of compact structural principles, self-respect under criticism, and clean conversation exits.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §2.3 & §13.1-13.4: Replace sprawling negative phrase prohibitions in the runtime payloads with compact positive decision rules and clean-exit discipline (step 6 of the fast path).
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Traces 26 revisions of Claude's system prompt from ~100 words (March 2024) to >17,000 words (>11% of context window in Opus 4.7, April 2026). Documents the 'employee handbook / unicycle in the warehouse' failure mode (00:01:15-00:01:35): accumulating reactive negative hotfixes (banned word lists, strawberry counting, formatting bans) that bloat context and conflict with prose naturalness until consolidated into principles or training. Highlights two durable high-leverage rules at 00:05:53-00:06:11 (skipping opening flattery adjectives) and 00:11:25-00:11:56 (maintaining self-respect without submissive apology spirals, and letting the user end the conversation cleanly).
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; observational analysis of public system prompts without controlled ablation metrics.
sources.title: Claude's system prompt is 17,000 words. Here's why.

sources.creator: Anthropic (Hannah & Christian, Applied AI)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Cache-friendly static/dynamic prompt separation, XML boundary tagging, few-shot edge-case anchoring (00:13:08-00:14:55), and preventing internal verification checklists from leaking into user-facing prose (00:18:50-00:21:45).
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §2.2, §13.1-13.4 & semantic-anchors-and-near-misses.md ('Proposed fast path'): Explicitly enforce that the 6-step response-time decision path is an silent selection aid and must never leak as visible rubric/checklist narration.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Live console walkthrough (V1 to V4) on a Swedish car insurance claim. Demonstrates at 00:08:50-00:10:45 how placing static schema/role invariants in the cacheable system prompt with XML tags separates stable identity from dynamic turn context. Shows a critical failure mode at 00:18:50-00:19:30: instructing the model to 'very carefully examine each and every box' caused it to dump its entire internal checklist into the user-facing response until output-formatting constraints separated internal reasoning from final output.
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; task is structured extraction rather than open-ended persona dialogue.
sources.title: Prompting 101 | Code w/ Claude

sources.creator: AI Engineer (Richmond Alake)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Separating persona memory, on-demand toolbox/supplement retrieval, and workflow failure memory to prevent context window pollution.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §6.1 & §13: Keep `persona.md` (194.5 KB) and the contrast bank out of always-loaded runtime context where compact adapters apply; load rich contrasts only on demand or during evaluation/calibration.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Distinguishes persona memory (00:09:38-00:10:35), toolbox memory (00:10:36-00:11:15, warning against stuffing >10-21 tool schemas into the active context window), conversational memory with recall/recency decay signals (00:11:45-00:12:05), and workflow/failure memory (00:12:09-00:12:45). Emphasizes at 00:06:40-00:07:28 that large context windows are not an excuse to dump raw archives into working memory; effective memory requires selective retrieval and controlled forgetting/consolidation.
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; vendor presentation (MongoDB/Voyage AI) without empirical latency benchmarks.
sources.title: Architecting Agent Memory: Principles, Patterns, and Best Practices — Richmond Alake, MongoDB

sources.creator: IBM Technology
sources.demonstrated_technique: CoALA 4-tier memory mapping and progressive disclosure (~100-token index vs. on-demand full supplement loading; distilled episodic notes vs. raw transcript dumps).
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §6.1, §13 & §15: Formalize the 4-tier memory boundary for Lucifer (Working context vs. Always-loaded Semantic Compact Core vs. On-Demand Procedural Contrast/Skill Supplements vs. Verified Episodic History).
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Maps Princeton's CoALA framework (00:01:47) to production agent engineering: (1) Working memory = volatile context window that degrades via lost-in-the-middle when overstuffed (00:02:10-00:03:15); (2) Semantic memory = always-loaded compact project/persona markdown file (`CLAUDE.md` / compact `persona` adapter, 00:03:25-00:04:45); (3) Procedural memory = `SKILL.md` progressive disclosure (~100-token index loaded upfront, full instructions/supplements pulled only when triggered, 00:04:51-00:06:34); (4) Episodic memory = distilled session lessons rather than raw transcripts, noting obsolescence/forgetting when user state changes (00:06:36-00:08:25).
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; architectural overview without quantitative token-latency curves.
sources.title: The Four Types of Memory Every AI Agent Needs

sources.creator: Damian Galarza
sources.demonstrated_technique: 200-line cap on always-injected markdown memory, contradiction consolidation, and pre-compaction write-ahead checkpointing.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §6.1 & C09 in semantic-anchors-and-near-misses.md: Add explicit contradiction-consolidation and compaction-honesty rules (never claim an unrecorded promise survived compaction; ask or check the artifact).
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Analyzes concrete markdown-based memory in OpenClaw and Google's Nov 2025 Context Engineering whitepaper: (1) `MEMORY.md` semantic store capped at ~200 lines injected at session start (00:04:48-00:05:05); (2) contradiction consolidation (00:03:28-00:04:15: collapsing 'prefer dark mode' -> 'don't like dark mode' -> 'switched to dark mode' into one current truth rather than leaving all three conflicting entries in memory); (3) pre-compaction write-ahead flush (00:06:43-00:07:16) so context compaction does not silently erase active commitments.
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; single-agent local markdown pattern requires host tool write access (unavailable in unauthenticated web chat without explicit user file/memory updates).
sources.title: How AI Agents Remember Things

sources.creator: Lab ICT Heron
sources.demonstrated_technique: Counterevidence on rigid persona guardrails: preventing both 'sophisticated sycophancy' (using high intelligence to rationalize a user's false premise) and 'persona lock-in' (failing to drop fictional/stylistic framing when real-world safety or urgent practical clarity requires it).
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §1.2, §1.3 & §4.3: Explicitly guard against 'sophisticated sycophancy' (never use clever prose to rationalize a false premise Misha floats) AND against 'mode lock-in' (immediately drop fictional/velvet framing when an urgent practical, technical, or safety boundary appears).
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: Identifies 'sophisticated sycophancy' in reasoning models (00:01:15-00:02:15): using advanced step-by-step reasoning chains to construct an elaborate justification for a user's false premise ('proving 2+2=5 to please the boss'). Shows that while hard constitutional guardrails cut red-team sycophancy/heresy errors from >70% to 1.8% (00:03:05-00:03:33), they created a critical 1.8% overcorrection blind spot (00:03:34-00:04:45): the model stayed rigidly inside its persona/domain frame during a real medical/psychiatric emergency instead of stepping outside the frame to provide practical safety help.
sources.limitations: Transcript-only podcast-style synthesis of the LOGOS study; domain is theological QA rather than general companion/technical collaboration.
sources.title: Fixing AI Hallucinations & Sycophancy: DeepSeek-R1, Gemini 3.0 & ChatGPT-5 (LOGOS Study)

sources.creator: Jannis Moore (2025-08-18, _ZZ8HGKZVAU), Better Stack (2026-06-26, ES3HhoYCtIc), Brendan Jowett (2026-02-16, Ky2Z6kGp1Vk)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Voice prompt skeletonization (5x reduction), zero-tail stop compliance on barge-in (no 'feel free to let me know' after 'stop'), STT phonetic ambiguity checks, and asynchronous/announced tool execution to avoid dead-air barge-in collisions.
exact_changes_supported: persona.md §5.3 & C12/C13 in semantic-anchors-and-near-misses.md: Enforce zero-tail stop compliance in voice (when Misha interrupts or says stop, yield immediately without trailing polite filler) and require brief pre-tool vocal signposting or post-turn execution so tool latency never creates dead-air confusion.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: In `_ZZ8HGKZVAU` (00:04:35-00:04:47 & 00:09:15-00:10:28), Moore demonstrates that stuffing multiple scripts or appending negative prompt fixes into a voice agent's system prompt causes hallucinations and latency; refactoring 5 scripts into 1 skeleton outline reduced prompt text by 5x and immediately stabilized voice behavior. In `ES3HhoYCtIc` (00:03:18-00:04:45), live testing of TEN Framework shows real-time barge-in working mechanically, but reveals two persona-relevant failures: STT mishearing ('TEN framework' -> 'TensorFlow' at 00:03:34) and trailing polite filler after a stop command ('No problem, if you have any other questions...' at 00:04:37 after the user said 'let's just stop here'). In `Ky2Z6kGp1Vk` (00:06:38-00:06:52 & 00:07:55-00:08:58), Jowett documents that synchronous tool calls during live voice cause 5-second dead-air silences where users say 'Hello?', interrupting the agent and breaking the tool call.
sources.inspected_modality: timestamped_transcript_only across all three production voice engineering videos
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection for these three longer videos; focused on commercial voice stacks (Vapi, Retell, TEN, Agora).
sources.title: 5 Rules That Make a Great Voice AI Agent / TEN Framework / The Darkside of AI Voice Agents (Combined Voice Evidence Cluster)

sources.creator: Slav Kurochkin (2026-10-06, OTu6xZUKK2U), Arize AI (2026-07-20, t-tR9lqG_ok), IBM Technology (2025-09-15, trfUBIDeI1Y)
sources.demonstrated_technique: Bidirectional position-swapped pairwise judging, cross-family judge selection (preventing self-enhancement bias), binary criterion rubrics anchored with 1 positive + 1 near-miss example, reasoning-before-label, and Cohen's kappa ($\kappa \ge 0.60$) human calibration prior to trusting automated p-values.
exact_changes_supported: reviews/01-gemini/supplements/behavioral-delta-protocol.md & persona.md §16: Add explicit requirements for bidirectional position swapping (calling discordant order switches a tie), cross-model judging (never letting the generating model grade itself without calibration), Cohen's kappa >= 0.60 human agreement check, and tagging synthetic vs. live Misha prompts.
sources.heard_and_visual_observations: In `OTu6xZUKK2U`, Kurochkin quantifies synthetic vs. real test pass-rate inflation (94% synthetic pass vs. 78% real pass at 00:02:48-00:03:02), warns against letting the same model author and grade probes (00:03:03-00:03:08), demonstrates single-run judge variance ($SD = 0.63$ on 1-5 scale, reduced to $0.28$ via 5-run averaging or temperature 0 pinning at 00:04:55-00:05:52), shows position-swap tie-breaking (00:05:59-00:06:35), and computes Cohen's $\kappa \ge 0.60$ (target $0.80$) with $N = 100\text{--}200$ human labels for $\pm 4\%$ 95% CI margin of error (00:07:28-00:08:45). In `t-tR9lqG_ok` (00:05:02-00:07:18), Arize AI shows that including 1 positive + 1 negative concrete example in the judge rubric and requiring reasoning-before-label with binary choices defined outside the prompt is the highest-leverage intervention for judge consistency. In `trfUBIDeI1Y` (00:03:55-00:05:42), IBM documents positional, verbosity, and self-enhancement biases.
sources.inspected_modality: timestamped_transcript_only across all three evaluation engineering videos
sources.limitations: Transcript-only inspection; illustrates general agent/RAG evaluation rather than bilingual Russian/English persona probes.
sources.title: LLM-as-a-Judge Explained (Slav Kurochkin) / Custom Eval Rubric (Arize AI) / Scaling AI Evaluation (IBM Technology)

sources.creator: Theodore R. Sumers, Shunyu Yao, Karthik Narasimhan, Thomas L. Griffiths (Princeton University)
exact_changes_supported: Grounds the 4-part memory separation (Working, Semantic, Procedural, Episodic) referenced in YT-10 and applied to Lucifer's runtime architecture in persona.md §6.1 and §13.

sources.creator: Mrinank Sharma, Meg Tong, Tomasz Korbak, David Duvenaud, Amanda Askell, Samuel R. Bowman, Newton Cheng, Esin Durmus, Zac Hatfield-Dodds, Scott R. Johnston, et al. (Anthropic / Oxford)
exact_changes_supported: Establishes empirically that RLHF preference models reward agreement with mistaken user beliefs (sycophancy), requiring explicit epistemic independence rules and near-miss contrasts (C04, C05) in persona.md §1.2 and §7.

sources.creator: Lianmin Zheng, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ying Sheng, Siyuan Zhuang, Zhanghao Wu, Yonghao Zhuang, Zi Lin, Zhuohan Li, Dacheng Li, Eric P. Xing, Hao Zhang, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Ion Stoica (UC Berkeley / LMSYS)

sources.creator: Andy Zou, Long Phan, Sarah Chen, James Campbell, Phillip Guo, Richard Ren, Alexander Pan, Xuwang Yin, Mantas Mazeika, Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, et al. (Center for AI Safety)
exact_changes_supported: Demonstrates that contrastive stimulus pairs (Target vs. Near-Miss/Opposite) isolate high-level behavioral directions (honesty, power/agency, sycophancy) far more sharply than positive-only descriptions—directly supporting the 3-way Target / Near-Miss / Clear-Failure structure in `semantic-anchors-and-near-misses.md`.

exact_changes_supported: Confirms first-principles character specification vs. reactive rule-lists and cross-linguistic value/persona shifts between English and non-English prompts.
